summary: Feed s160_double is degraded: 100% of packets are untagged so required VLANs 10,20 are missing, and 24.8% of TCP sessions (38/153) are one-way. NDR cannot segment by VLAN or reassemble sessions, severely reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Upstream SPAN destination or packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery. 100% of packets arrived untagged, so required VLANs 10 and 20 are invisible. Common when switch SPAN is set to strip VLAN or broker ingress/egress port is configured to remove tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires VLANs 10,20 for segmentation and detection logic. Without tags it cannot filter, correlate, or apply VLAN-aware policies, effectively blind to those segments.

recommended_fix.why: Retain 802.1Q tags end-to-end from TAP/SPAN through packet broker to NDR so VLANs 10 and 20 are delivered intact for correct classification.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of many TCP sessions is reaching the tool (38 of 153 sessions, 24.8% one-way). Indicates asymmetric visibility - separate TAP/SPANs for each direction not aggregated to the same tool port, or broker load-balancing hashing that splits forward and reverse flows to different outputs.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions for TCP reassembly, state tracking and behavioral detection. One-way sessions cause incomplete flows, missed detections, and false alerts, severely degrading NDR efficacy.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR port using bidirectional flow-aware hashing so full sessions are reconstructed.
